newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's 1996 year better than expected - Chatset.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's 1996 year better than expected - Chatset.

text.p: The Lloyd's insurance market looks to have performed better than expected in 1996 with profits of over 700 million stg expected, according to market analysts Chatset.
The year, which has been affected by pressure on insurance rates, saw good loss frequency but also a sharp fall in premium income.
Chatset increased its profit estimates for previous years, with its latest forecast for 1994 standing at 1.177 billion stg and 1995 at 985 million stg.
This would make 1994 the most profitable in Lloyd's history.

Chatset noted 1996 was almost free of major catastrophes and that serious aviation disasters -- the mid-air collision at Delhi and the TWA crash off Long Island, New York -- and the Eurotunnel fire are not expected to impact the market.
The 1996 profit figure is based on net premium income of 2.02 billion stg.
Chatset said around 50 to 60 percent of 1996 premium income will have been received at this stage.

Its income forecast was sharply down on 1994 and 1995 at 5.8 and 5.7 billion stg respectively and it attributed this to inception day accounting, introduced into the 1995 account, pressure on rates and loss of business.
